subject: Logic
title: The Ship of Theseus
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Ship of Theseus usable.

hook.text: Replace every plank on a ship, one by one. When you're done, is it still the same ship?

buildup.text: Theseus's ship was preserved by replacing rotting wood. Over time, no original material remained.

discovery.text: If someone rebuilt the old planks into a second ship, which one is the real Ship of Theseus?

twist.text: Your body replaces most cells every decade. Are you the same person you were at ten years old?

climax.text: Identity might not live in material. It could be in form, continuity, or something harder to define.

quiz.question: What does the Ship of Theseus paradox question?
